- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to forecasted values post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to counteract mean reversion.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts are prone to lag; adjust by adding 1–2% upward bias to align with true outcome trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment polarity shift.
